dateline: Washington / Brussels / Ankara / Vilnius / Normandy — June 7, 2026
heroHeadline: PUTIN & ZELENSKY HOLD SEPARATE CALLS WITH TRUMP AHEAD OF NATO ANKARA SUMMIT (JUL 7–8); TRUMP SET TO TEST NATO UNITY AT SUMMIT; LITHUANIA FIRST AT 5% GDP; UK: RUSSIA COULD ATTACK NATO BY 2030
heroSubtitle: As of June 7, 2026, the NATO-US tracker marks 31 days to the Ankara Leaders' Summit (July 7–8) with three compounding developments from June 5–7. On June 7, Lithuania became the first NATO member to exceed the Hague 5% GDP target — the Seimas approved a record €4.79B defense budget (5.38% of GDP), nine years ahead of the 2035 deadline, driven by the EUCOM June 3 confirmation of zero US submarines and drones to NATO's force pool and Lithuania's direct Russian border threat. On June 6, Defense Secretary Hegseth attended the 82nd D-Day anniversary at Ouistreham, Normandy, and held a bilateral with French Armed Forces Minister Vautrin — both agreed on urgency of 'NATO 3.0' transition, with Hegseth demanding 'Europe must be the first to provide for its own conventional defense.' Simultaneously, Politico reported NATO allies are negotiating a €70B Ukraine military aid package for Ankara (Germany-led, combining EU SAFE loans and PURL contributions; four diplomatic sources, no official confirmation). On June 5, UK PM Starmer delivered the starkest NATO threat assessment in years: allied intelligence assessments indicate Russia could attack NATO territory as soon as 2030; UK will publish a 10-year defense investment plan before Ankara. The June 18 NATO Defense Ministers meeting in Brussels — the last pre-Ankara ministerial — has nuclear sharing expansion on its confirmed agenda (Polish Defense Minister Kosiniak-Kamysz, June 4). BALTOPS 26 maritime exercise continues (June 4–19, 15 nations, ~20 ships) as the visible operational expression of the new NATO 3.0 posture: European navies bearing greater share as US naval contributions retreat from the force model.
